# Translate Foreign Documents and Everyday Signs with Gemini

**Hook:** Point your phone at a Japanese menu, a French letter or a German street sign, and Gemini can read the image, translate the text, and answer your follow-up questions — all in plain English. This guide shows you exactly how, even if you've never opened the app before.

## Before you start
- A **Google account** — the same one you use for Gmail, YouTube or Android works fine.
- The **Gemini app** on your phone (iOS or Android), or just open the Gemini website in a browser. Either works for this task.
- A **smartphone with a working camera** is the easiest option. A laptop with a webcam also works.
- The **free plan is enough** for everyday translation. A paid Google AI subscription (Google offers several tiers — names and prices change, so check the app for the latest) may unlock bigger or faster models, but you don't need it to start.
- Allow about **5 minutes** for your first try. Good lighting and a steady hand make a real difference to photo quality.

## Step 1 — Open Gemini and start a fresh chat
Tap the **Gemini app icon** on your home screen — it looks like a four-pointed star shape, mostly in shades of blue and white. If you can't find it, swipe up to open your app drawer and search "Gemini". If you'd rather use a computer, open your browser and go to the Gemini website. Either way, you'll land on a **chat screen** with a text box near the bottom and a short greeting at the top, ready for your first message.

💬 Example: (no typing yet)

You'll know it worked when you see the empty chat box, a blinking cursor, and no error messages.

## Step 2 — Attach a photo of the sign, menu or document
Look near the **text box** for a small **camera icon** 📷 or a **"+" button**. Tap it, and a small menu usually appears with options like "Camera" (to snap a new photo) and "Photos" or "Gallery" (to pick one you already took). Hold your phone flat and steady over the document, and try to fill the frame with the text so nothing important gets cut off. If you can't see a camera icon, look for a paperclip or attachment symbol instead — the exact spot varies by app version and device.

💬 Example: (no typing yet)

You'll know it worked when a small **thumbnail of your photo** appears next to the text box, waiting to be sent.

## Step 3 — Ask Gemini to translate the photo
With the photo attached, **tap into the text box** and write what you need. Be specific about both the language and what you want — *"translate to English"* is a good start, but adding a follow-up question usually gets a more useful answer. Then tap the **send button** — usually a paper plane icon ✈️ on the right edge of the text box. Wait a few seconds while Gemini reads the image, then replies with the translation and any extra notes you asked for.

💬 Example: "Translate this menu to English. After the translation, list the three cheapest main courses and tell me which ones look vegetarian."

You'll know it worked when a translated version of the text appears in the chat, in plain English, within roughly 10–20 seconds.

## Step 4 — Read the result and ask follow-up questions
Scroll through the first reply — it usually contains a clean translation. If a dish name, sign or letter still feels unclear, **type another question in the same chat**. Your photo stays attached, so Gemini keeps using it as context. This is where Gemini feels different from a basic translation app: you can ask things like *"what's the spiciest option?"* or *"summarise what this letter is asking me to do"* without uploading anything new.

💬 Example: "What does the word 'konbini' mean here, and is the dish at the top of the page likely to contain nuts?"

You'll know it worked when Gemini answers your new question using the same photo — without you having to send it again.

## Step 5 — Try Gemini Live for hands-free translation (optional)
If you're standing in front of a sign or menu and don't want to type, Gemini Live lets you **point your camera and talk**. Look around the chat area for a button labelled **"Live"** or an icon that looks like a **microphone or sound wave**. Exactly where it sits depends on your app version — it may be near the text box, in a side menu, or tucked inside a settings panel. Tap it, allow camera and microphone access if asked, and a viewfinder opens. Point your phone at the text, speak your question, and Gemini listens, looks, and replies out loud — no typing needed.

💬 Example: (say this out loud) "I'm looking at a Japanese train station sign — what does it say, and which platform do I need for Shinjuku?"

You'll know it worked when Gemini **speaks the translation back to you** while the camera stays open. If you can't find the Live button, your app version may not have it yet — the typed photo method in Steps 2–4 still works perfectly.

## Common mistakes
- **The photo is blurry or angled.** Fix: hold the phone flat, fill the frame with the text, and tap to focus on the document before snapping. Good lighting matters more than a fancy camera.
- **You ask for a translation but forget to say which language you want.** Fix: always write *"translate to English"* — without it, Gemini may reply in the original language.
- **You expect 100% accuracy on handwritten notes.** Fix: typed text and printed signs translate best; handwriting, very old fonts, and crumpled paper can confuse the AI. Treat the result as a helpful first pass, not a certified translation.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Travel becomes less stressful — you can read street signs, restaurant menus, train tickets and even letters from family overseas without fumbling through a phrasebook.
- **For your business or work:** Translate customer emails, product labels, supplier invoices or international contracts for a first read — then bring the important ones to a qualified human translator for sign-off.
- **If you're just getting started:** Pick **one thing in another language** sitting in your house right now — an old letter, a product label, a souvenir menu — and run it through Step 3 tonight.

## What Gemini cannot do here
Gemini **reads and translates the image**, but it is not a certified translator. For legal documents, immigration papers, medical instructions or anything with real consequences, treat the output as a draft and verify with a qualified human translator before acting on it.

## Try it now
In the next two minutes: open the Gemini app, snap a photo of any piece of text you can see right now — a cereal box, a bill, a sign out the window — and ask *"translate to English and summarise the key points"*. You'll have your first translation before your cup of tea is ready.
